# Testament of Gad — 9
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Gad's testament is the hatred counterpart to Zebulun's compassion. He confesses something raw: he hated Joseph for nine months with the full force of his will, and he wanted to destroy him.

**1** He said, at age 125:

**2** I loved my father. I loved my brothers. But Joseph — I hated with everything I had.

**3** The spirit of hatred had taken hold of me. I wanted to erase him from the earth the way a bull tears through a field. Nine months of that.

**4** But the LORD wouldn't let me do it. When Joseph came out to the fields to check on us, my spirit rose up in fury — I threw stones at him. And when he ran from me, I was glad. The spirit of hatred wanted to kill him, but God kept me from finding him alone.

**5** So hear me now, sons. Hatred is ruin. It poisons everything.

**6** Here is what hatred does: the hater hates everything the beloved person does — even good things. The hated man keeps the law of God? The hater doesn't praise him for it. The hated man fears God and delights in righteousness? The hater still cannot love him. Truth is loathsome to the hater. The hater celebrates when the beloved stumbles. The hater loves gossip, loves pride, loves darkness.

**7** Hatred sins against God. It refuses to hear his commands about loving your neighbor. When a brother fails, hatred runs to broadcast it everywhere — it wants judgment and punishment and death. Even against a servant: hatred looks for any excuse to bring him down.

**8** And hatred feeds on envy. The longer the envied person prospers, the more the hater wastes away.

**9** Understand this: love can call back the dead; hatred will kill the living. Love works with the law of God — patiently, for salvation. Hatred works with Satan — quickly, for death.

**10** Hatred makes small things enormous. It turns light into darkness. It calls sweet things bitter. It teaches slander. It kindles war. It fills the heart with poison.

**11** So: drive hatred out. Cling to the love of God.

**12** Here is how: righteousness drives out hatred. Humility destroys envy. A just and humble person is ashamed to do what's wrong — not because someone is watching, but because his own heart convicts him.

**13** Don't speak against someone when they're suffering. Don't say it to their face. If they repent, forgive them. If they keep sinning against you — forgive them anyway. Leave the settling of accounts to God.

**14** And this: if a man sins against you seventy times in a day, forgive him seventy times. A man with a good heart who sins is not the same as a man with an evil heart. The repentant one, God forgives immediately. The shameless one — forgive him from your heart and let God handle the rest.

**15** When someone prospers more than you — pray for their prosperity. It's better for you that way. When someone rises higher than you — don't envy them. Everyone dies. Praise God for what he gives to everyone.

**16** Seek God's judgment. Your mind will find rest.

**17** Love one another. Bear each other's weaknesses with patience. God delights in brothers who are unified and in hearts that choose love.

**18** Then he had them carry his bones to Hebron. He ate, he drank, he was glad. He covered his face and died.

---
*End of Testament of Gad*
